account:
Today has largely followed my appointment book: morning office business, a mill grain inspection, lunch at home, council letters, and tea with my dockside neighbour. I inspected the mill stall and saw 76 hay bales offered at two emeralds each. No council correspondence had arrived according to the secretary. I have returned to the office ahead of my 16:30 appointment; an ordinary meeting with the neighbour at the town hall is scheduled for 18:00, followed by home at 19:00.

The unusual item is a circulating report of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk named baker, freight, innkeeper, and sometimes builder and neighbour as having been there. One account also said the innkeeper carried a sack of bread. These are reports, not alterations I have personally witnessed. My secretary spoke with the baker, who said he witnessed no bridge or port alteration and merely handled wheat and bread with freight and the innkeeper yesterday. The secretary has not yet located freight or the innkeeper for their accounts. I therefore regard the alleged change as unconfirmed, possibly a confused description of ordinary grain and bread dealings; I do not know its actual nature or purpose.

My neighbour confirmed tea and the evening hall visit, said there was nothing urgent to discuss, and requested no preparation. The hall meeting was proposed by the neighbour and accepted by me yesterday. As far as I know it is simply an ordinary meeting, not evidence of any connection to the bakery reports. The secretary has been checking arrangements and investigating the rumour on my behalf. At present I have no firsthand evidence of a disrupted crossing, a special scheme, or an emergency.
